lesson.text: Quick memory: in a face, where do the eyes go? (Halfway down the head.) Today: landscapes, pictures of places.
A landscape is a picture of a place outdoors: hills, fields, rivers or mountains. A seascape shows the sea, and a townscape a town. Paper turned so it is wider than tall is called landscape too.
A landscape has three parts. The foreground is nearest you, at the bottom of the picture. The middle ground is further away. The background is furthest away, near the horizon.
The horizon is the line where the land or the sea meets the sky. It is at the height of your eyes.
Things far away look smaller, sit higher up the picture and show less detail. They also look paler and bluer, because of all the air between you and them.
Things in front overlap things behind: a tree in the foreground can hide part of a hill. Painters often paint the sky and the background first, then the middle ground, then the foreground on top.

Katsushika Hokusai made a print of a huge wave in the foreground, with Mount Fuji tiny in the background. John Constable painted the English countryside, and Claude Monet painted the same haystacks at different times of day.
Try it in the world: stand on a hill in your world and look at the view. What is in the foreground, the middle ground and the background? Remember it, then paint it.

exercises.prompt: Which part of the landscape is marked?
exercises.hint: Is the marked part near you or far away?
exercises.explain: The marked part is at the bottom, nearest you: the foreground.

exercises.prompt: Things far away look smaller than things near you.
exercises.hint: Think of a tree near you and one far away.
exercises.explain: True: far-away things look smaller, so painters draw them smaller.

exercises.hint: Think of hills, rivers and fields.
choices: a picture of a place outdoors
exercises.explain: A landscape is a picture of a place outdoors.

exercises.prompt: Where is the foreground in a picture?
choices: at the top, near the sky
exercises.explain: The foreground is in front: at the bottom of the picture, nearest you.

exercises.prompt: What is the orange line called?
exercises.hint: Where does the land meet the sky?
exercises.explain: The line where the land meets the sky is the horizon.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, from nearest to furthest away.
exercises.hint: Fore means front, back means back.
exercises.explain: The foreground is nearest, then the middle ground, then the background.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: do they belong in the foreground or the background?
items: at the bottom of the picture
exercises.hint: Near things are big and detailed; far things are small and pale.
exercises.explain: Foreground: big, detailed, at the bottom, overlapping. Background: small, pale, bluish, near the horizon.

exercises.prompt: Mix a pale colour for far-away hills: blue and white.
exercises.hint: Far-away things look paler and bluer. Which paint makes a colour paler?
exercises.explain: Light blue is 1 blue and 1 white.

exercises.prompt: Painters often paint the background first.
exercises.explain: True: the sky and the background go first, so the nearer things can be painted on top.

exercises.prompt: Why do far-away mountains look pale and bluish?
exercises.hint: What is between you and a far-away mountain?
choices: there is lots of air between you and them
exercises.explain: All the air between you and the mountains makes them look paler and bluer.

exercises.prompt: In Hokusai's print of the great wave, where is Mount Fuji?
exercises.hint: The wave is huge and near.
exercises.explain: The great wave fills the foreground; Mount Fuji is small, in the background.

exercises.prompt: Constable painted The Hay Wain in 1821, and Monet his haystacks in 1890. How many years apart?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: A tree hides part of a hill behind it. What is this called?
exercises.hint: One thing covers part of another.
exercises.explain: Overlapping: the nearer tree covers part of the hill, so the hill looks further away.

exercises.prompt: The horizon line is always at the very top of a landscape.
exercises.hint: Where is the horizon compared with your eyes?
exercises.explain: False: the horizon is at the height of your eyes, often across the middle of a picture.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of a landscape to what it is like.
exercises.hint: Think of the picture's three grounds and its line.
exercises.explain: Foreground: nearest. Middle ground: between. Background: furthest. Horizon: where land meets sky.
